title: KRATOS: Context-Aware Cell Type Classification and Interpretation using Joint Dimensionality Reduction and Clustering

problem.claim: Single-cell RNA-sequencing analysis commonly uses a pipeline that reduces dimensions, clusters cells, and extracts distinguishing gene panels.

gap.claim: The pipeline performs its steps independently and neglects dependencies among the steps and marker genes or gene panels.

contributions.claim: KRATOS integrates single-cell RNA-sequencing analysis by jointly optimizing dimensionality reduction and clustering, followed by an interpretability step.
KRATOS uses a compact integrated workflow to extract marker genes intended to discriminate a target cluster and distill mechanisms guiding cluster membership.
The authors provide code and datasets through a public repository.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that KRATOS extracts marker genes that better discriminate the target cluster and distill underlying mechanisms guiding cluster membership.
The authors report that KRATOS is 5.62% superior to GCE and 3.31% better than ACE on AUROC measured with a kernel-SVM classifier.
The authors report open-sourcing their code and datasets.

narrative_sequence.summary: Single-cell RNA-sequencing analysis commonly follows a three-step workflow.
The workflow treats its stages and marker genes independently despite their dependencies.
KRATOS jointly optimizes dimensionality reduction and clustering and adds interpretability as an integrated pipeline.
The authors report improved marker discrimination and better AUROC than two named baselines.
The authors report releasing code and datasets.

source_observation.claim: The described workflow jointly optimizes dimensionality reduction and clustering before interpreting cluster membership.

interpretation.claim: When pipeline stages are interdependent, integrating their objectives may produce representations that are more useful for downstream interpretation.

application.claim: Consider joint optimization when designing multi-stage analytical pipelines whose intermediate outputs constrain later explanations.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether joint optimization is preferable for datasets, objectives, or settings beyond those evaluated.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the joint optimization objective or model architecture.
The abstract does not describe the datasets, experimental protocol, or statistical uncertainty.
The abstract does not provide the absolute AUROC values or clarify the comparison denominator for the reported percentage improvements.
